title: Patient Guide | House of Zen
description: For Michigan card holders: what to bring, purchase and possession limits, taxes, caregivers, visiting patients, public use and work. As of October 2026.
lede: For people who already hold a medical card: how Michigan’s rules read, as of October 2026. This is general information, not medical or legal advice.
note: The House of Zen live menu mentions valid medical patients. Please call us to confirm whether and how we can serve medical card holders today.

blocks.html: Registered patients buy from licensed provisioning centers by showing their registry card and photo ID. Patients must present a valid registry card and a valid driver license or government-issued photo ID at the time of purchase.

Keep them within reach when you are out, too. To be protected from arrest, a patient or caregiver must show police a valid registry card plus photo ID, and a card counts only if it is reasonably accessible where you are. An application or physician form is not a temporary card.

items: Buying: up to 2.5 ounces a day and 10 ounces a month per patient, checked in the statewide monitoring system.
Holding: up to 2.5 ounces of usable marijuana, with infused products counted by a set equivalency.
The equivalency: 1 ounce of usable marijuana equals 16 ounces of solid infused product, 7 grams of gaseous infused product, or 36 fluid ounces of liquid infused product.
Growing: if no caregiver grows for you, up to 12 plants kept in an enclosed, locked facility.

blocks.html: Medical marijuana sold to registered patients is not subject to Michigan’s 10% excise tax; only the 6% sales tax applies. Purchases by visiting patients count as medical sales for this purpose.

A caregiver must be at least 21, consent to a criminal background check and have no disqualifying convictions, and receives a separate caregiver card for each patient served. Under the statute, each patient may have only one caregiver, and a caregiver may assist no more than 5 registered patients.

A caregiver may possess 2.5 ounces of usable marijuana and equivalents for each connected patient, and 12 plants in an enclosed, locked facility for each patient who has allowed the caregiver to cultivate. Daily purchase limits apply per connected patient.

Michigan honors out-of-state medical cards. A visiting patient with a valid, unexpired card from another state plus photo ID may buy at a licensed medical provisioning center, within the same purchase limits.
The medical law does not allow smoking marijuana in any public place, and the Court of Appeals has held that a car parked in a lot open to the public counts.

A Michigan medical card does not stop a private employer from disciplining or firing an employee for marijuana use, though a court has held that such patients cannot be denied unemployment benefits for a failed test.
These descriptions cover format only. They say nothing about what any product will do for you.

items: Flower and pre rolls: the dried plant, loose or already rolled, usually smoked.
Vaporizers: devices that heat oil or flower into a vapor you inhale.
Edibles: foods made with cannabis, which you eat.
Concentrates: extracts that hold a lot in a small amount.
Topicals: creams, balms and oils applied to the skin.
CBD products: products built around CBD, one of the plant’s compounds. Read the label for THC as well.

blocks.html: For anything about your health, please talk with your physician. For the program’s own word on any of this, go to the state’s Cannabis Regulatory Agency. Still applying? See Getting a Medical Card.
